title: NO KINGS. NO SILENCE. Anne Arundel Has Something to Say.

NO KINGS. NO SILENCE.
June 14: Anne Arundel Has Something to Say.

Saturday, June 14, 2025
Gather at 7:00 PM | March begins at 7:30 PM
Waugh Chapel Towne Centre, Gambrills, MD 

In America, we don't bow to would-be kings — and we won’t start now.

So, we’re showing up — visibly, loudly, and together.

The Route:
We’ll begin at Waugh Chapel Towne Centre, then march down Route 3 (Crain Highway). At the Route 3 & Route 424 intersection, we’ll cross and head back on the opposite side of the highway.

This Is a Peaceful Demonstration
This is a nonviolent, community-centered protest. We are here to uplift, not escalate. All participants are expected to act with dignity, care, and courage.

The flag doesn’t belong to Trump. It belongs to the people.
We’re not watching history happen — we’re making it. Join us.

title: Disappeared in America Host Call
description:
**Trump thinks he can disappear people. We’re building a movement to prove him wrong.**

In America, the government doesn’t get to grab people off the streets, skip the courtroom, and send them straight to a foreign prison. That’s not who we are. But that’s what happened to Kilmar Abrego Garcia, Rui Marras, Juan Maldonado Zuniga, and so many others.

Join us on **Tuesday, June 17 at 8:00 PM ET** for a host call to learn why this moment matters, how sheriffs play a central role in this crisis, and what you can do to push back — starting in your own community.

This meeting is designed to provide support for Disappeared in America hosts and ensure that your action successfully lays out the stakes: how this administration is undermining the rule of law, how local law enforcement is being pressured to comply, and how people like you can help expose and resist these abuses on June 26 and beyond.

#DisappearedInAmerica is a campaign led by a growing coalition of immigrant rights, faith, rule of law, and pro-democracy organizations.
People will be gathering in front of courthouses and other public spaces, holding posters of those who have disappeared, and taking group photos to be shared across social media. We must demonstrate that Americans across the country stand in solidarity with those who are vulnerable under the Trump administration and oppose any violations of due process.


**Register now and be part of the resistance to lawless power.**

title: Defend Our Immigrant Communities: Say NO to 287(g)!
description:
On Tuesday, June 17 at 8AM, the Miami City Commission is set to vote on whether to enter a 287(g) agreement with ICE. This program would deputize local police to act as immigration enforcement agents—giving them power to stop, question, arrest, and detain people they suspect of immigration violations during everyday policing.

This decision would make Miami the largest city in Florida to join the 287(g) task force model—at a time when communities across the country are reeling from increased raids, deportations, and anti-immigrant policies.

We say NO.

Miami is a city where nearly 60% of residents are foreign-born and over 70% are Latino/a/x. 287(g) would criminalize and terrorize the very people who make this city vibrant, resilient, and full of life. It doesn’t make us safer—it makes our communities more vulnerable to profiling, detention, and deportation.

This vote was already deferred once, but our response hasn’t changed:
We will be at City Hall, loud and clear, demanding that our city reject this collaboration with ICE.

🗓 Tuesday, June 17th — 8:00 AM
📍 Miami City Hall – 3500 Pan American Dr, Miami, FL 33133

Bring signs, wear white for unity, and show up in solidarity. This is a moment for people power.

#No287g #StopTheDeportations #PeoplePower #Miami

title: Organize the Church Clergy Call: State of the People National Assembly in Baltimore
description:
### **Organize the Church Clergy Call: State of the People National Assembly, Baltimore**  
**Friday, June 13 • 7:00 PM ET • Virtual**

**Black Church PAC, Black Church Freedom Fund, and LIVE FREE USA** invite Black clergy, gospel artists, worship leaders, sacred creatives, and faith organizers to a national call to organize the Church ahead of the **State of the People National Assembly**, June 19–21 in Baltimore.

This is not just a meeting. It is a clarion call.  
A national assembly is forming — rooted in truth, strategy, and Black liberation.  
As civil rights leaders, cultural influencers, and frontline organizers prepare to gather, the Black Church must take its rightful place: visible, vocal, and vital.

---

### On this call, we will:
1. **Brief you on** *Organize the Church: State of the People Power Tour, Baltimore* — what’s happening during the National Convening and why it matters.  
2. **Share how we can organize the Church** to spiritually anchor the Assembly, serve in worship and hospitality roles, and bring moral clarity to the public square.  
3. **RSVP to secure your spot at the Convening:** [https://stateoftheppl.com/baltimore](https://stateoftheppl.com/baltimore) — and select “volunteer” if you’d like to serve on the Host Committee.

---

### **About the Assembly**  
The *State of the People National Assembly* is the culminating stop of a 10-city tour — held on Juneteenth weekend in Baltimore. Inspired by the 1972 Gary Convention, it will unite national Black leaders, civil rights voices, artists, and everyday people to confront harm, build power, and shape a vision for Black futures.

This is a moment of spiritual urgency and generational opportunity.  
**Join us. Stand with us. Help lead us.**

title: Gather: an Interdependence Day Potluck
description:
Gather: an Interdependence Potluck on Wednesday, July 2nd | 6:00–8:30pm at Wilshire Park (4116 NE 33rd Ave, Portland 97212)

Brown Hope and Lulove Healing are hosting a Gather: an Interdependence Day Potluck, an invitation to build community in the spirit of interdependence and collective resilience.

Gather with us to share an intimate moment of giving and receiving care, respect, and love. Join us in nourishing our bodies and souls with a shared meal, and you’re encouraged to bring your favorite dish! There will be vegan and gluten free options. 

We’ll have interactive icebreaker activities to help people meet and socialize. Experienced song circle facilitators will lead us in songs and drumming that honor our values of freedom, justice, healing, and liberation.

Gather is also an opportunity to shine a light on the truth about this nation’s long history of injustice. July 4th is a day that carries a lot of traumatic the United States. The holiday often glazes over the slavery, colonialism, and genocide that this nation was built upon, and the present day inequities that persist due to the lack of accountability and resolution. 

Brown Hope Founder and CEO, cameron whitten, will perform a live reenactment of the 1852 speech “What to the Slave is Your 4th of July?” by civil rights leader Frederick Douglass.

We’ll have a facilitated group dialogue after the speech and brainstorm ideas about how to increase our collective power and foster a more interdependent Portland community that’s actively working towards racial justice. 

Gather is free and open to the public. We welcome people of all racial backgrounds, as well as uplifting Black, Brown, and Indigenous leadership on our journey towards collective liberation.

#GatherPDX #BeTheFire

title: July Monthly Meeting – Special Guest: Brajan Funes on TPS and Migrant Justice

sponsor.name: Camel City United Indivisible North Carolina

description:
Join Camel City United Indivisible for our monthly community meeting as we welcome special guest Brajan Funes, a local organizer and advocate who will speak about Temporary Protected Status (TPS) and the urgent fight for migrant justice.

📣 TPS is under threat.
For over 25 years, tens of thousands of Honduran nationals have lived and worked in the U.S. under TPS — including many of our neighbors in North Carolina. Their futures hang in the balance as their protections expire this July.

“We’ve had 25 years of them giving us TPS. And for them to say that they’re going to cancel it, it’s a big hit,” says G., a longtime NC resident currently in sensitive immigration proceedings.
“You have a hope for all those years that they might give you residency.”

Together, we’ll discuss:

What TPS means for our communities

The risks facing families if TPS is revoked

How we can support advocacy efforts for permanent protections

🗣️ This meeting is open to all. Learn, connect, and take action as we continue building a just and inclusive Forsyth County.
